sentenceSets.sentence: The informal perquisites of the position were never listed but were among the primary reasons the role was sought.

answerChoices.reasoning: A prerogative is an exclusive power attached to an office and exercised as authority over others, whereas these are unstated advantages that made people want the job for themselves.
An emolument is the compensation formally attached to an office, and the sentence marks these as never appearing on any list, which separates them from the stated pay.
An amenity is a comfort available to everyone in a place, while these belong to the position itself and explain why that position in particular was sought.
A concession is something reluctantly yielded in a negotiation, and nothing here was bargained for; the sentence presents them as simply coming with the role.
Duties would be reasons to avoid a post, not the primary reasons candidates pursued it.
Rituals are customary practices one performs, and the sentence describes things people wanted to receive.
Credentials are the qualifications a candidate brings to a post rather than advantages the post confers.
Hazards would deter applicants, contradicting the statement that these drew people to the role.
Punishments cannot be among the primary reasons anyone sought a position.
Sanctions are measures imposed against someone and would repel candidates rather than attract them.
A burden is something one would rather not carry, the opposite of an inducement to take the job.

sentenceSets.sentence: A perquisite of the royal huntsman's office was the right to keep the hides of every deer taken in the king's forest.

answerChoices.reasoning: A stipend is money paid out at regular intervals, while what the huntsman receives here is the right to keep a particular thing that comes to hand in the course of the work.
A bounty is a reward posted for each kill in order to encourage killing, whereas this right simply attaches to holding the office.
A tithe is a share owed by others to a church or a lord, and in this sentence it is the huntsman himself who keeps what he takes.
Spoil is what is seized from a defeated enemy, and this is a customary entitlement of a servant of the crown going about his ordinary duties.
A warrant is the document authorizing an act, not the advantage the officeholder gets to keep.
A fiefdom is land held in return for service, and what is described is the hides of the deer rather than any grant of ground.
Livery is the uniform issued to a household's servants, which is supplied to them rather than taken by them in the field.
A commission is the appointment that confers the office, while the hides are one of the things the office brings with it.
Penance is a punishment undertaken for sin, the opposite of a right worth having.
A levy is an exaction imposed on people, and the huntsman is gaining here rather than paying.
Forfeiture is the loss of something, which contradicts a right to keep the hides.

sentenceSets.sentence: She turned the offer down because the salary was flat and the only perquisite worth naming was a parking space.

answerChoices.reasoning: An incentive is dangled to induce particular performance, but a parking space comes with the job regardless of how she does it.
An allowance is a sum of money set aside for expenses, and what the sentence names is a physical space supplied rather than cash to spend.
A bonus is an extra payment tied to results, and the sentence has already dealt with money by calling the salary flat.
An inducement is offered specifically to bring a candidate in, while the parking space is part of what the post carries and was plainly not enough to move her.
A stipulation is a condition written into an agreement, not something of value the employer supplies.
A formality is a procedural step, and a parking space is a tangible benefit rather than a piece of process.
A requirement is something demanded of her, which would not be described as worth naming alongside the salary.
A courtesy is a politeness extended by other people, whereas the parking space is a standing feature of the package she was offered.
A deduction takes money away and could never be listed among the attractions of an offer.
A liability is a burden of exposure, not something the employer offers to sweeten a flat salary.
A drawback is a disadvantage, which makes no sense as the one thing about the offer worth mentioning favorably.
